records.summary: Millennium bim publishes his dated CV. It lists him at the Banco de Moçambique (Banco Central) from 1976 to 1992, ending as a member of its board of administration 1989-1992, then as executive director of Banco Comercial de Moçambique, S.A. from 1992 to 2000 and of Banco Internacional de Moçambique, S.A. from 2000 to 2015, then at the insurer Seguradora Internacional de Moçambique, S.A. from 2015 to 2021. On the ownership of the bank he joined in 2000, the Institute of Developing Economies company file for Mozambique sets out the holdings in Millennium BIM as '66.69% BCP Internacional II, Sociedade Unipessoal, SGPS', '17.76% Estado Moçambicano', '4.95% INSS - Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social', '4.15% EMOSE - Empresa Moçambicana de Seguros, SARL', '1.08% FDC - Fundação para o Desenvolvimento da Comunidade' and '5.37% Gestores, Técnicos e Trabalhadores', and describes the parent Banco Comercial Português as 'a Portugal-based, privately owned bank'. So the holding is mixed and the majority holder is stated to be private. Millennium bim's own 2008 annual report prints the same shareholder table during his time there: 'BCP Internacional II, SGPS, Lda. 4.941.393 66,69%', 'Estado Moçambicano 1.271.440 17,16%', 'INSS - Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social 366.846 4,95%', 'EMOSE - Empresa Moçambicana de Seguros, S.A.R.L. 307.319 4,15%'.

held.note: The Banque Centrale de Mauritanie document back end at bo.bcm.mr answered HTTP 500 on its JSON:API root, so its biographies could not be listed; needs a hand check. The two Financial Afrik appointment pieces that were read (the January 2020 profile of governor Mohamed Cheikh El Kebir Moulaye Taher and the September 2020 piece on the bank's new directors and senior advisers) name only central bank, ministerial and PROCAPEC posts, with no private employer and no ownership wording.

Two officials not worked at the earlier round were opened. The George Washington University Africa Finance and Trade profile of governor Ibrahim L. Stevens gives Bank of England, International Growth Centre at the LSE, Rwanda's Ministry of Finance and a GIZ project - all public or academic. The Wikipedia page for Silvanus Nicol-Cole gives only the Bank of Sierra Leone 1962-1970 and the IMF 1970-1972. Neither names a private financial employer. The Bank of Sierra Leone's 2022 annual report carries board and management profiles that have not been read.

Two pages on the appointment of governor Américo d'Oliveira dos Ramos were read - the Forbes África Lusófona piece and the Central Banking report. Both describe him only as a former finance minister and give no employer list, so no private financial employer is named and nothing about ownership. The Association of African Central Banks profile page for the Banco Central de São Tomé e Príncipe has not been read and may carry the governor's and administrators' career lists.

MBf Bank Limited's key disclosure statement for 2025 states the bank 'is a 100% owned subsidiary of MBf Asia Capital Corporation Holdings Limited', incorporated in Hong Kong, and lists its directors, among them Dr Aisake Valu Eke, but gives no occupations or prior roles for any of them. The Pacific Islands Forum biography of Eke gives the Ministry of Finance and National Planning, two teaching posts and the Legislative Assembly, and does not mention the National Reserve Bank of Tonga. The Wikipedia page for governor Sione Ngongo Kioa (2013-2022) gives central planning, the IMF, the Ministry of Finance, a cyclone reconstruction project, Leiola Duty Free Shops and diplomatic posts - a duty free retailer is not financial. Matangi Tonga's notice of the two deputy governors appointed gives only Reserve Bank service and an IMF secondment. What would settle it is whether Eke, an MBf Bank Limited director, ever served at the National Reserve Bank of Tonga.

The Reserve Bank of Vanuatu's current board page gives full biographies for chairman Andrew Kauisiama, governor August Letlet, Nikunj Soni and Gregoire Nimbtik; every employer named is a government body, a regional or donor organisation or a university, and the page does not state the ownership of Air Vanuatu or Vanuatu Terminal Services, where Kauisiama sat on boards. The previous board members page is only a list of governors and general managers 1981-2010 with no biographies. The bank's Press Release No 02 of 2014 on the appointments of Branan Karae and Michael Hililan gives Reserve Bank posts and IMF secondments only. The 2024 annual report has board and management profiles that have not been read.

Two Bolivian regulator documents were read for the ownership of Banco de Cochabamba S.A. and Compañía Boliviana de Seguros S.A., the two employers on the Banco Central de Bolivia's CV for general manager Jaime Valencia Valencia whose status is open. The Superintendencia de Bancos 1999 annual report puts Banco de Cochabamba S.A. only under the headings 'ENTIDADES EN PROCESO DE LIQUIDACIÓN' and 'ENTIDADES EN LIQUIDACIÓN', with the resolution 'Banco de Cochabamba S.A. R.SB. 422/94 25.11.94', and says nothing about who owned it. ASFI's Libro Historia Tomo II, read from character 100,000 to 200,000, mentions the bank four times, all about the 1994 liquidation - 'Un efecto casi inmediato de la promulgación de la Ley de Bancos es la liquidación en 1994 de: BancoSur y Banco de Cochabamba' - and never names a shareholder; Compañía Boliviana de Seguros does not appear in that stretch at all. Supreme Decree 23881 of 11 October 1994 is about the Banco Central de Bolivia repaying depositors of banks in forced liquidation and uses no ownership wording. Nothing read states private ownership, so no record is filed. ASFI's Libro Historia Tomo I, covering the earlier period when the bank was founded and operating, has not been read.

The years still do not decide it. The United States country study chapter on Sudanese banking lists the banks the government set up with their founding years - Agricultural Bank of Sudan 1959, Industrial Bank of Sudan 1961, Sudanese Estates Bank 1966 - records the 1970 Nationalization of Banks Act and the 1974 opening to foreign banks, but never mentions a National Bank of Sudan or a Workers National Bank, so it cannot say which institution Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir led in 1980-1982 nor who owned it. The Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker banking paper, read to character 100,000, gives only aggregate counts - forty commercial and specialised banks, twelve wholly or majority government owned - and names neither bank; it does state of a different bank that 'The CBoS intervened to bail out ONB, which became 85% owned by the Central Bank'. The Central Bank of Sudan's own About page covers 1956-1960 only and lists no banks. The second half of the Sudan Transparency paper has not been read and may carry the per-bank ownership list.

searched_no_result: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu, 'Board of Directors - Current Board Members' page, the four biographies of Andrew Kauisiama, August Letlet, Nikunj Soni and Gregoire Nimbtik: every employer named is public, academic or a donor programme.
Reserve Bank of Vanuatu, 'Board of Directors - Previous Board Members' page: a bare list of general managers and governors 1981-2010, no biographies.

Reserve Bank of Vanuatu, Press Release No 02 of 2014, 'RBV Announces Recent Appointments', the career paragraphs for Branan Karae and Michael Hililan: Reserve Bank posts and IMF secondments only, no employer before joining the bank.

Matangi Tonga, 'Two Deputy Governors appointed for Nat'l Reserve Bank of Tonga', the career paragraphs for Ungatea Latu and Lata Tangimana: over 25 years at the bank each, plus an IMF secondment for Latu; no outside employer.

MBf Bank Limited, Key Disclosure Statement 2025, ownership and directors sections: ownership stated as a 100% subsidiary of MBf Asia Capital Corporation Holdings Limited, Hong Kong; the five directors are listed with no occupations or prior roles.

Pacific Islands Forum, leaders page for Hon. Dr 'Aisake Valu Eke, career section: Ministry of Finance and National Planning, Tupou Tertiary Institute, Christ's University in the Pacific, Legislative Assembly; no bank.

Wikipedia, 'Sione Ngongo Kioa', career section: central planning, IMF, Ministry of Finance, cyclone reconstruction, Leiola Duty Free Shops, Tonga Chamber of Commerce, diplomatic posts, then Governor 2013-2022; the only private employer is a duty free retailer, not financial.

Financial Afrik, 25 January 2020, 'Mauritanie: Mohamed Cheikh El Kebir nouveau gouverneur de la Banque centrale (BCM)', career section: BCM departments, PROCAPEC, Ministry of Employment 2007-2008, Ministry of Economy 2019; PROCAPEC's legal status is not stated.

Financial Afrik, 29 September 2020, 'Mauritanie: la Banque centrale étoffe son organigramme', the list of new directors general and senior advisers: no career history and no private employer for any of them.

Forbes África Lusófona, 'Banco Central de São Tomé e Príncipe tem novo governador', on Américo d'Oliveira dos Ramos: finance minister 2014-2018 and a 2019 criminal case later dropped; no employer list.
Central Banking, 'São Tomé appoints new central bank governor': describes Ramos only as a former finance minister, no career history.

George Washington University Africa Finance and Trade, profile of Ibrahim L. Stevens, career section: Bank of England about ten years, Bank of Sierra Leone director of research 2008-2010 on secondment, deputy governor 2014 and governor from November 2023, International Growth Centre at the LSE, Rwanda's Ministry of Finance, a GIZ project; nothing private.
Wikipedia, 'Silvanus Nicol-Cole': Bank of Sierra Leone deputy governor 1962-1966, governor 1966-1970, IMF alternate executive director 1970-1972; no other employer.
Banco de Moçambique, CV of Maria Esperança Mateus Majimeja, career section: Ministry of Cooperation 1991-1992 then Banco de Moçambique from 1993 to administrator in 2022; no private employer.

Millennium bim, CV of Moisés Jorge, career section: two Portuguese construction firms 1991-1993, then Millennium bim and BCP from 1994 to 2015; the central bank is not named, so it is not a revolving-door record.
Central Bank of Sudan, English 'About' page: the bank's own 1956-1960 history; no list of Sudanese banks and no mention of the National Bank of Sudan or the Workers National Bank.

United States country study of Sudan, banking chapter: founding years for the state development banks, the 1970 Nationalization of Banks Act and the 1974 opening to foreign banks; neither the National Bank of Sudan nor the Workers National Bank is mentioned.
Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker, banking paper, first 100,000 characters: aggregate bank counts and Omdurman National Bank's ownership; neither of Nimir's two banks appears.

Superintendencia de Bancos y Entidades Financieras de Bolivia, 1999 annual report, 'Entidades en Proceso de Liquidación' section: Banco de Cochabamba S.A. appears only as a bank in liquidation, with no ownership or shareholder statement.
ASFI, Libro Historia Tomo II, characters 100,000 to 200,000: the 1994 liquidation of BancoSur and Banco de Cochabamba, no shareholders named; Compañía Boliviana de Seguros does not appear.
Bolivia, Supreme Decree 23881 of 11 October 1994 on the Banco Central de Bolivia repaying depositors of banks in forced liquidation: no ownership wording at all.
